key_concepts: A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
Electromagnetic induction occurs when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
A basic generator uses a coil of wire around an iron core rotated near a magnet.
A generator does not create energy; it forces movement of existing electric charges.
Electric motors and generators both require electric and magnetic forces.
Turbines are large wheels rotated by water, wind, or steam to drive generators.
A commutator in a generator changes AC to DC in the armature winding.
Common energy sources include biofuel, wind, water, heat, and solar.
